planTheory.hypothesis: Assignment targets two distinct sub-skills bundled under "multiplication": (1) automatic recall of x2/x5/x10 facts, and (2) translating equal-groups word problems (boxes of pencils, rows of stars) into multiplication sentences. Both need direct, comparable practice today. Reina's engagement theory (evidenceCount 23+, confidence ~0.73-0.92) shows strong positive weight for puzzle (5.0) and speed (5.0) framing, near-zero/negative for competition, control, calm, and generic quiz shells (generated-baseline: 20% completion, dislike, frustration 0.554). Per Keller's ARCS and the child's own nextExperiment (variable: mechanic, arms unset), this board holds academic targets/question count/difficulty/evidence contract constant across two routes while varying MECHANIC (puzzle-lock manipulation vs. timed-speed run) to test which drives higher completion/engagement without adding competitive pressure or heavy control demands.

planTheory.intervention: Deep beneath an old observatory, a vault of frozen starlight has locked away its glittering treasure using ancient multiplication seals. Reina has found two entrances carved into the vault door: a Puzzle Gate of interlocking gears and a Comet Gate that only opens for those who move at comet-speed. Both paths lead to the same starlit treasure room, but only one gate will open first tonight.
falsifyCriteria: Real child evidence contradicts the theory.
